subject: chemistry
title: Enthalpies of solution and hydration
key_idea: When an ionic solid dissolves, the lattice breaks up into gaseous ions and the ions are then hydrated. The **enthalpy change of solution** equals the energy to break the lattice plus the **enthalpies of hydration** of the ions. Highly charged, small ions give large lattice and hydration enthalpies.

blocks.text: Dissolving has two stages. Energy is needed to separate the ions. Energy is released when water molecules bond to them.

items.meaning: The enthalpy change when 1 mol of a solute dissolves completely in a solvent, so that the ions no longer interact.
The enthalpy change when 1 mol of gaseous ions dissolves in water to form 1 mol of aqueous ions.
The enthalpy change when 1 mol of ionic lattice breaks up into gaseous ions. It is endothermic.

items: Hydration is exothermic. Polar water molecules are attracted to the ions: the δ− oxygen to cations and the δ+ hydrogens to anions.
Breaking the lattice is endothermic. It is the opposite of lattice formation.
Dissolving can be endothermic or exothermic overall, depending on which of the two is bigger.
A solid is more soluble when ΔsolH is exothermic or only slightly endothermic. Entropy also matters (see Entropy).
Hydration of gaseous ions is exothermic.
Breaking the lattice is endothermic.
ΔsolH is the net effect of the two.

blocks.text: The cycle links the solid and the aqueous ions by two routes. The direct route is dissolving. The other goes through gaseous ions.

blocks.label: Enthalpy change of solution
where: lattice enthalpy of formation is negative, so its minus sign gives a positive term
ΣΔhydH = the hydration enthalpies of the cation and the anion, each times the number of moles of that ion

items.text: Put the solid, NaCl(s), on the left and the aqueous ions, Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), on the right. Put the gaseous ions below.
Solid to gaseous ions: +787 (lattice dissociation). Gaseous ions to aqueous ions: the two hydration enthalpies.
Na⁺ hydration is −406 kJ mol⁻¹ and Cl⁻ hydration is −364 kJ mol⁻¹. ΔsolH = 787 − 406 − 364 = +17 kJ mol⁻¹.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the enthalpy change of solution of sodium chloride from the lattice enthalpy and the hydration enthalpies.
diagram.question: For NaCl: lattice enthalpy of dissociation = +{d} kJ mol⁻¹, ΔhydH of Na⁺ = −{c} kJ mol⁻¹, ΔhydH of Cl⁻ = −{a} kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔsolH.
working: ΔsolH = lattice dissociation + hydration of Na⁺ + hydration of Cl⁻

items: Energy level diagrams show the same information: the gaseous ions at the top, the solid and aqueous ions below, and arrows for each step.
To find a missing term, such as a hydration enthalpy, rearrange the cycle.
For a compound with a 2+ ion or two anions, such as MgCl₂, multiply by the number of moles of each ion.
ΔsolH = lattice dissociation + hydration of the ions.
Multiply each hydration enthalpy by the number of ions in the formula.
Check the sign of lattice enthalpy: formation is negative, dissociation positive.

sections.heading: Effect of ionic charge and radius

blocks.text: Both the lattice enthalpy and the hydration enthalpy depend on the charge and size of the ions in the same way. The attraction is stronger when the ions have a higher charge density.

rows: More exothermic: stronger attraction between ions
More exothermic: stronger attraction to water molecules
Less exothermic: water molecules are further from the charge

items: Mg²⁺ has a much more exothermic hydration enthalpy than Na⁺, because it has twice the charge and is smaller.
Down Group 2 and Group 1 the cations get larger, so both the lattice and hydration enthalpies become less exothermic.
Solubility trends come from how fast each of these two changes with ionic size.
High charge and small size give the largest enthalpies.
The trend applies to both lattice and hydration enthalpies.
ΔsolH depends on the difference between the two large numbers.

checks.q: Define the enthalpy change of hydration.
checks.a: The enthalpy change when 1 mol of gaseous ions dissolves in water to form 1 mol of aqueous ions.

checks.q: The lattice enthalpy of dissociation of MgCl₂ is +2526 kJ mol⁻¹. The hydration enthalpies are Mg²⁺ −1920 and Cl⁻ −364 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔsolH.
Explain why the hydration enthalpy of Mg²⁺ is more exothermic than that of Ca²⁺.
checks.a: Mg²⁺ is smaller than Ca²⁺ with the same charge, so its charge density is higher and it attracts water molecules more strongly.

items: Definitions are required for enthalpy change of solution and enthalpy change of hydration. Details of infinite dilution are not required.
Use simple ionic solids such as NaCl and MgCl₂ for the cycles and calculations.
Use energy cycles and energy level diagrams to calculate ΔsolH, ΔhydH and lattice energy.
Give the effect of ionic charge and radius on the values of lattice energy and enthalpy change of hydration.
Use the symbols ΔHhyd and ΔHsol.
Explain, in qualitative terms, how ionic charge and ionic radius change the size of an enthalpy change of hydration.
Define the enthalpy of hydration.
Use cycles to calculate enthalpies of solution for ionic compounds from lattice enthalpies and enthalpies of hydration, as part of Born–Haber work.
